note.question: How can a principal use selective feedback, rather than money, to persuade an agent to continue a costly search when only the principal can evaluate the search outcomes?
note.overview: A principal who privately observes realized search outcomes commits to a dynamic stopping and messaging policy, whereas an agent who bears search cost decides whether to continue after each message. The optimal policy is an information-design mechanism satisfying the agent’s sequential best responses.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Before search, the principal commits to stopping and messaging policies. At each opportunity the principal observes past outcomes and chooses stop or continue; if continuing, the principal sends a message; the agent updates beliefs and chooses stop or pay cost c to search once more; the terminal payoff is split r and 1−r. The principal wants more search because the agent pays the cost but shares the terminal return. The principal’s stop/continue action itself conveys information even before an explicit message.
